self-graded-verdict.ruleText: A verdict produced by the Implementer about its own task is a `self-graded-verdict` finding at `blocker` severity, regardless of how convincing the output reads

unnamed-evaluator.ruleText: Name the mechanism that discharges the Evaluator role before execution starts; forbid execution with an unnamed evaluator

ungrounded-task.ruleText: Derive every task from at least one VCC; a task tracing to no VCC is an `ungrounded-task`

unexecuted-condition.ruleText: Ensure every VCC is covered by at least one task; a VCC with no task is an `unexecuted-condition`

task-cycle.ruleText: Express dependencies as a directed acyclic graph over Task IDs; a cycle is a `task-cycle` finding at `blocker` severity

concurrent-write-conflict.ruleText: Group ready tasks into waves for concurrent dispatch; forbid two tasks in one wave writing the same artifact, which is a `concurrent-write-conflict`

parallel-scope-collision.ruleText: **Collaboration identity complete when concurrent mutation applies**; authoritative future write scopes, distinct lanes, and exact fences are present without path inference; current local leases are required only for local mutation-capable projections

stale-collaboration-fence.ruleText: **Collaboration identity complete when concurrent mutation applies**; authoritative future write scopes, distinct lanes, and exact fences are present without path inference; current local leases are required only for local mutation-capable projections

delivery-authority-unjoined.ruleText: **Reviewed delivery authority is exact when protected integration applies**; one current `delivery-authorized` receipt binds the unchanged reviewed revision, scope, claim, lease epoch, fence, ledger revision, and review/check evidence without reopening authoring or granting deployment authority

canonical-base-drift.ruleText: **When additive concurrent authoring is requested, scoped lane admitted and preserved**; joined receipts bind exact source/scope, cloud/local/shared-state digests, target/atomic result, final active claim evidence, zero candidate-caused collateral mutation, `authoringAdmission: admitted`, and claim-plus-local-lease revalidation at first consumption

scope-admission-collision.ruleText: **When additive concurrent authoring is requested, scoped lane admitted and preserved**; joined receipts bind exact source/scope, cloud/local/shared-state digests, target/atomic result, final active claim evidence, zero candidate-caused collateral mutation, `authoringAdmission: admitted`, and claim-plus-local-lease revalidation at first consumption

unattributed-lane-ambiguity.ruleText: **Collaboration identity complete when concurrent mutation applies**; authoritative future write scopes, distinct lanes, and exact fences are present without path inference; current local leases are required only for local mutation-capable projections

admission-snapshot-stale.ruleText: **When additive concurrent authoring is requested, scoped lane admitted and preserved**; joined receipts bind exact source/scope, cloud/local/shared-state digests, target/atomic result, final active claim evidence, zero candidate-caused collateral mutation, `authoringAdmission: admitted`, and claim-plus-local-lease revalidation at first consumption

unsafe-candidate-target.ruleText: **When additive concurrent authoring is requested, scoped lane admitted and preserved**; joined receipts bind exact source/scope, cloud/local/shared-state digests, target/atomic result, final active claim evidence, zero candidate-caused collateral mutation, `authoringAdmission: admitted`, and claim-plus-local-lease revalidation at first consumption

local-only-cross-device-lease.ruleText: **Collaboration identity complete when concurrent mutation applies**; authoritative future write scopes, distinct lanes, and exact fences are present without path inference; current local leases are required only for local mutation-capable projections

collateral-lane-mutation.ruleText: **When additive concurrent authoring is requested, scoped lane admitted and preserved**; joined receipts bind exact source/scope, cloud/local/shared-state digests, target/atomic result, final active claim evidence, zero candidate-caused collateral mutation, `authoringAdmission: admitted`, and claim-plus-local-lease revalidation at first consumption

admission-runtime-conflation.ruleText: Keep scoped authoring admission, runtime readiness, and lifecycle readiness as independent results; never turn preserved disjoint work or an occupied runtime into a false global verdict

candidate-lane-orphaned.ruleText: **When additive concurrent authoring is requested, scoped lane admitted and preserved**; joined receipts bind exact source/scope, cloud/local/shared-state digests, target/atomic result, final active claim evidence, zero candidate-caused collateral mutation, `authoringAdmission: admitted`, and claim-plus-local-lease revalidation at first consumption

state-without-reason.ruleText: Record a reason on every transition to `failed`, `blocked`, or `abandoned`; an unexplained terminal state is a `state-without-reason` finding

oversized-task.ruleText: Split a task that exceeds its budget rather than raising the budget; a persistent overrun is a decomposition defect, and raising the bound hides it

unsurfaced-result.ruleText: Forbid a return that asserts success without a named check and a recorded result; the Evaluator judges surfaced output only, so an unsurfaced pass is indistinguishable from no pass

unenumerated-change.ruleText: Enumerate artifacts changed even when the change is incidental; an unenumerated change is invisible to the concurrent-write and blast-radius rules

self-escalated-capability.ruleText: Forbid self-escalation: an Implementer that needs a wider class returns `blocked` with the reason, and the Orchestrator re-dispatches with a new grant. Widening a grant mid-task is a `self-escalated-capability` finding at `blocker` severity

out-of-scope-write.ruleText: State the declared write scope before dispatch; a write outside it is an `out-of-scope-write` finding

ungated-irreversible-operation.ruleText: Require an explicit Operator decision per irreversible operation; forbid a standing or session-scoped approval for irreversibility, because a standing approval is indistinguishable from no gate

unbounded-task.ruleText: State all four bounds before dispatch; a task dispatched with any bound unstated is an `unbounded-task` finding at `blocker` severity

budget-raised-under-pressure.ruleText: Forbid raising a bound to rescue a failing task within the same run; re-decompose instead, because a bound raised under pressure is a bound that no longer bounds

unrecorded-consumption.ruleText: Record consumption against every bound in the return, whether or not the bound was approached; unmeasured consumption cannot be budgeted next time

fix-without-witness.ruleText: Every bug-fixing task first adds a check that fails on the unfixed state; a fix with no failing-first check is a `fix-without-witness` finding

unproven-property.ruleText: Derive a property from every correctness property stated in the specification; a stated property with no executable test is an `unproven-property` finding

evidence-without-run.ruleText: Forbid emitting an Evidence Reference for a check that was not run in this task

unresumable-run.ruleText: Persist run state — task states, transitions with reasons, Evidence References, findings, budget consumption — outside working context after every terminal transition

assumed-operator-decision.ruleText: Forbid inferring, defaulting, scheduling, or simulating an Operator decision; an absent decision is a `blocked` state, never an assumed yes

unreviewed-release-candidate.ruleText: Require a current Runtime Review Receipt before prompting and a separate authenticated human decision for the exact candidate and target before deployment

dependency-closure-drift.ruleText: **Candidate closure exact**: canonical source, all transitive dependencies, policy, target, review, artifact, manifest, and candidate digests agree

authorization-evidence-unjoined.ruleText: **Receipt chain joined**: Integration, Runtime Review, Candidate, Authorization Interaction, Human Authorization, Deployment, State Reconciliation, Live Verification, Publication, and Rollback receipts join by exact digest where each stage applies

authorization-interaction-unjoined.ruleText: **Human authorization exact**: the interaction receipt proves the configured transport, browser dependency, exact challenge response, and authenticated actor; the authority adapter records the same human decision for that candidate and target

duplicate-release-controller.ruleText: **Controller singular and idempotent**: one target-scoped controller owns deployment; duplicate dispatch resolves to the same result or fails closed

production-authorization-drift.ruleText: Invalidate the affected receipt chain on any identity movement; cancel or retire stale unapproved runs rather than retargeting, rebuilding, or reusing authorization

post-authorization-rebuild.ruleText: **No drift or rebuild**: current evidence still matches the authorized candidate byte-for-byte; otherwise authorization is invalid and forward deployment remains blocked

state-reconciliation-unverified.ruleText: **State reconciled**: state changes are bounded and idempotent, direct readback matches expected counts and content, and code and state rollback dispositions remain separate

immutable-origin-unverified.ruleText: **Transports proven separately**: immutable origin, required public routes, authoritative state readback, browser behavior, client-cache convergence, and publication each carry their own evidence where applicable

public-route-unverified.ruleText: **Transports proven separately**: immutable origin, required public routes, authoritative state readback, browser behavior, client-cache convergence, and publication each carry their own evidence where applicable

client-cache-convergence-unverified.ruleText: **Transports proven separately**: immutable origin, required public routes, authoritative state readback, browser behavior, client-cache convergence, and publication each carry their own evidence where applicable

publication-before-live-verification.ruleText: Publish mirrors only after the Live Verification Receipt exists; remove only clean, integrated, completion-proven task lanes and preserve all unrelated work

cleanup-ownership-unproven.ruleText: **Keep / port / drop inventory closed**: every pre-existing non-canonical lane or worktree is classified by exact identity; `keep` items remain preserved, `port` items integrate before candidate sealing, and `drop` items are removed only with value-closure proof plus cleanup authority

integration-order-cycle.ruleText: Build a directed acyclic graph from declared unit dependencies; a cycle is an `integration-order-cycle`, and integrating a unit before a dependency is `integration-before-dependency`

integration-before-dependency.ruleText: Build a directed acyclic graph from declared unit dependencies; a cycle is an `integration-order-cycle`, and integrating a unit before a dependency is `integration-before-dependency`

canonical-frontier-unverified.ruleText: Require the protected merge revision and its exact-canonical checks before advancing the frontier; a green task head alone is `canonical-frontier-unverified`

duplicate-change-reintegrated.ruleText: Classify each unit as `pending`, `already-integrated`, `superseded`, `integrated`, or `blocked`; forbid reintegrating an equivalent change or replacing newer canonical behavior with an older unit

stale-candidate-frontier.ruleText: **Candidate closure exact**: canonical source, all transitive dependencies, policy, target, review, artifact, manifest, and candidate digests agree

runtime-readiness-unproven.ruleText: Emit `runtime-readiness-unproven` at `blocker` severity when a required receipt, join, budget, check, evaluator, dependency, or boundary proof is absent or stale

undesigned-criterion.ruleText: Verify both chain seams are closed before dispatching any task derived from them; an uncovered criterion is an `undesigned-criterion` and an ungrounded design element is an `ungrounded-design-element`

ungrounded-design-element.ruleText: Verify both chain seams are closed before dispatching any task derived from them; an uncovered criterion is an `undesigned-criterion` and an ungrounded design element is an `ungrounded-design-element`

requirement-introduced-downstream.ruleText: Forbid an execution task deciding structure or introducing behaviour absent upstream; either is a `requirement-introduced-downstream` at `blocker` severity and returns to the owning phase

stale-downstream-artifact.ruleText: Reject a task list whose upstream artifact revision no longer matches the artifact it was derived from; a stale downstream artifact is a `stale-downstream-artifact` and re-derivation precedes dispatch

phase-advanced-without-approval.ruleText: Require a recorded Operator decision for each seam crossing before execution starts; an unapproved crossing is a `phase-advanced-without-approval` and an absent decision is a `blocked` state

seam-elided.ruleText: Permit a collapsed or reordered chain only where both seams still carry joins; a missing coverage obligation is a `seam-elided` at `blocker` severity, however small the change

executionRuleCatalog.scope--neutrality-contract#1: **Neutral**: name agents, roles, and mechanisms by their function, never by a brand. Where a concrete tool is shown, it appears only under a heading or block whose own text contains the words "reference implementation", and may be swapped for any equivalent.
executionRuleCatalog.scope--neutrality-contract#2: **Agnosticity**: every rule is evaluated from document content and parsed frontmatter only — never from file names, directory layout, or downstream mirrors. Examples use placeholders (`[...]`) rather than real identifiers.
executionRuleCatalog.scope--neutrality-contract#3: **Complementary**: this set owns **execution**. Authoring — what a PRD, TAD, or ADR must contain, the Readiness Ladder, the Rule ID scheme, and the authoring-domain finding vocabulary — is owned by the **PRD, TAD & ADR Guidelines** companion set. This set does not restate those rules; it names them and consumes them.
executionRuleCatalog.module-index#2: `execution-contract` — what an agent receives, what it must surface, and what closes a task
executionRuleCatalog.module-index#3: `human-in-the-loop-gates` — which decisions an agent must not make alone
executionRuleCatalog.boundary-with-the-authoring-set#1: Treat a baselined document pair with zero open `blocker` findings as the entry precondition for execution; forbid starting execution against an unbaselined or blocker-carrying specification
executionRuleCatalog.boundary-with-the-authoring-set#2: Reuse the authoring set's Rule ID derivation and finding recording contract verbatim; forbid a second, parallel conformance vocabulary
executionRuleCatalog.boundary-with-the-authoring-set#3: Forbid either set redefining a Finding Type the other owns; the conformance vocabulary is the union of the two enumerations
executionRuleCatalog.boundary-with-the-authoring-set#5: Close execution with a verified Integration Receipt before invoking a release controller; forbid an Implementer task from preparing, authorizing, or deploying a release
executionRuleCatalog.agent-roles--independence#1: **The Evaluator must be a different mechanism from the Implementer.** This is the one role separation that survives every collapse.
executionRuleCatalog.agent-roles--independence#2: Independence is **mechanical**, not organisational: a deterministic check, a hook, or a separate evaluating process satisfies it; a different job title applying the same judgement does not
executionRuleCatalog.agent-roles--independence#3: A solo operator satisfies the rule by delegating the verdict to a check they do not adjudicate, and violates it by reading their own output and declaring it done
executionRuleCatalog.agent-roles--independence#5: The Operator never collapses into any other role, because an inferred approval is not an approval
executionRuleCatalog.agent-roles--independence#6: A verdict produced by the Implementer about its own task is a `self-graded-verdict` finding at `blocker` severity, regardless of how convincing the output reads
executionRuleCatalog.agent-roles--independence#7: Name the mechanism that discharges the Evaluator role before execution starts; forbid execution with an unnamed evaluator
executionRuleCatalog.agent-roles--independence#8: Route every completion verdict through the Evaluator; forbid a task transitioning to a terminal success state on the Implementer's assertion alone
executionRuleCatalog.agent-roles--independence#9: Record which role produced every state transition, so a self-graded verdict is detectable after the fact rather than only in the moment
executionRuleCatalog.specification-chain-phases#1: Verify both chain seams are closed before dispatching any task derived from them; an uncovered criterion is an `undesigned-criterion` and an ungrounded design element is an `ungrounded-design-element`
executionRuleCatalog.specification-chain-phases#2: Reject a task list whose upstream artifact revision no longer matches the artifact it was derived from; a stale downstream artifact is a `stale-downstream-artifact` and re-derivation precedes dispatch
executionRuleCatalog.specification-chain-phases#3: Forbid an execution task deciding structure or introducing behaviour absent upstream; either is a `requirement-introduced-downstream` at `blocker` severity and returns to the owning phase
executionRuleCatalog.specification-chain-phases#4: Require a recorded Operator decision for each seam crossing before execution starts; an unapproved crossing is a `phase-advanced-without-approval` and an absent decision is a `blocked` state
executionRuleCatalog.specification-chain-phases#5: Permit a collapsed or reordered chain only where both seams still carry joins; a missing coverage obligation is a `seam-elided` at `blocker` severity, however small the change
executionRuleCatalog.specification-to-task-bridge#1: Derive every task from at least one VCC; a task tracing to no VCC is an `ungrounded-task`
executionRuleCatalog.specification-to-task-bridge#2: Ensure every VCC is covered by at least one task; a VCC with no task is an `unexecuted-condition`
executionRuleCatalog.specification-to-task-bridge#3: Record the source criterion and VCC identifiers on each task; forbid a task list that cannot be joined back to the specification
executionRuleCatalog.specification-to-task-bridge#4: Report bridge coverage as covered VCCs over total VCCs; forbid claiming a task list is complete without that ratio
executionRuleCatalog.specification-to-task-bridge#5: Forbid introducing a requirement at task-authoring time: a task that needs behaviour absent from the specification is a specification defect, so return it to the authoring loop rather than inventing scope inside the task list
executionRuleCatalog.specification-to-task-bridge#6: Re-derive the task list whenever a VCC changes; a task list outrunning its specification produces work no rung will ever credit
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#1: Assign each task exactly one Task ID, stable while the task's own text is unchanged
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#2: Limit hierarchy to two levels: a task and its sub-tasks; forbid a third level, which trades comprehensibility for the illusion of precision
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#3: Record the Task ID on every state transition, every Evidence Reference, and every finding raised during that task
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#4: Expose exactly four provider-neutral root operations: `claim(scope)`, `continue(claim)`, `integrate(candidate)`, and `retire(claim)`; each emits a typed digest-bound receipt, and adapters must not add authority-bearing aliases or compatibility operations
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#5: Treat dependency edges as the group's only ordering authority; a shared task identity or semantic label never creates a shared branch, worktree, lease, claim, fence, review identity, or handoff
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#8: Require admission and every later mutation batch to preserve pre-existing lanes and join current cloud and local authority with joined Admission and Preservation Receipts plus operation receipts; these receipts grant no cleanup, runtime, release, deployment, or authority outside their exact work unit
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#9: Keep authoring ownership, review readiness, and delivery authorization as separate capabilities: `review-ready` closes source mutation, while a later explicit `delivery-authorized` compare-and-swap transition may authorize protected integration of only the unchanged reviewed revision and write scope; it must bind the current claim, lease epoch, fence, ledger revision, review and check evidence, emit an idempotent receipt, never reactivate authoring or grant deployment authority, and isolate provider-specific review and integration behavior behind replaceable adapters
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#12: Size every task so its completion is verifiable by a check named in advance; forbid a task whose completion is judged by inspection
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#13: Split a task that exceeds its budget rather than raising the budget; a persistent overrun is a decomposition defect, and raising the bound hides it
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#14: Forbid a task with no verifiable outcome; documentation-only tasks state the artifact and the check that confirms it exists and conforms
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#15: Express dependencies as a directed acyclic graph over Task IDs; a cycle is a `task-cycle` finding at `blocker` severity
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#16: Derive readiness from the graph: a task is ready when every dependency is in a terminal success state
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#17: Group ready tasks into waves for concurrent dispatch; forbid two tasks in one wave writing the same artifact, which is a `concurrent-write-conflict`
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#18: State the graph explicitly; forbid inferring order from list position alone, which silently couples ordering to formatting
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#19: Forbid any state named `done`, `complete`, or equivalent that an Implementer may set; `verified` is the only success state and only the Evaluator sets it
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#20: Record a reason on every transition to `failed`, `blocked`, or `abandoned`; an unexplained terminal state is a `state-without-reason` finding
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#21: Forbid transitioning out of a terminal state except by an explicit re-derivation that resets the task to `not-started` and records why
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#22: Never infer a state from an artifact's existence; a file appearing on disk is not a verdict
executionRuleCatalog.execution-contract#1: What an Implementer receives, and what it must return.
executionRuleCatalog.execution-contract#2: An Implementer must surface, in its own output, everything the Evaluator needs:
executionRuleCatalog.execution-contract#3: Forbid a return that asserts success without a named check and a recorded result; the Evaluator judges surfaced output only, so an unsurfaced pass is indistinguishable from no pass
executionRuleCatalog.execution-contract#4: Forbid an Implementer reading state the Evaluator cannot see and relying on it in a verdict request
executionRuleCatalog.execution-contract#5: Enumerate artifacts changed even when the change is incidental; an unenumerated change is invisible to the concurrent-write and blast-radius rules
executionRuleCatalog.execution-contract#6: Surface the constraint violations the task caused, not only the ones it found; self-reporting is cheaper than detection and is the only path that scales
executionRuleCatalog.tool-permission--blast-radius#1: Grant the narrowest class that completes the task; forbid granting a class the task does not name a use for
executionRuleCatalog.tool-permission--blast-radius#2: Forbid self-escalation: an Implementer that needs a wider class returns `blocked` with the reason, and the Orchestrator re-dispatches with a new grant. Widening a grant mid-task is a `self-escalated-capability` finding at `blocker` severity
executionRuleCatalog.tool-permission--blast-radius#3: Require an explicit Operator decision per irreversible operation; forbid a standing or session-scoped approval for irreversibility, because a standing approval is indistinguishable from no gate
executionRuleCatalog.tool-permission--blast-radius#4: Forbid boundary-crossing capability in any task; promotion is the Deploy Boundary's job, and a task that reaches a delivered surface is a `deploy-boundary-breach` under the authoring set's enumeration
executionRuleCatalog.tool-permission--blast-radius#5: Forbid transmitting project content, credentials, or user data to an external endpoint during execution unless the Operator requested that specific transmission
executionRuleCatalog.tool-permission--blast-radius#6: State the declared write scope before dispatch; a write outside it is an `out-of-scope-write` finding
executionRuleCatalog.per-task-budgets#1: State all four bounds before dispatch; a task dispatched with any bound unstated is an `unbounded-task` finding at `blocker` severity
executionRuleCatalog.per-task-budgets#2: Forbid raising a bound to rescue a failing task within the same run; re-decompose instead, because a bound raised under pressure is a bound that no longer bounds
executionRuleCatalog.per-task-budgets#3: Record consumption against every bound in the return, whether or not the bound was approached; unmeasured consumption cannot be budgeted next time
executionRuleCatalog.per-task-budgets#4: Aggregate per-task consumption into a per-run total and compare it to the estimate in the specification's token budget; a run exceeding its specification's budget is an economics finding, not a surprise
executionRuleCatalog.per-task-budgets#5: Keep retries idempotent: a retried task must not double-apply its own prior partial work
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#1: Every task states its **named check** before dispatch, phrased as it is invocable
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#2: Every code-bearing task adds or extends automated tests covering the behaviour it introduces
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#3: Every bug-fixing task first adds a check that fails on the unfixed state; a fix with no failing-first check is a `fix-without-witness` finding
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#4: Every task runs the project's existing verification lane, not only its own new check; a task that passes its own check while breaking a neighbour's is a regression the Evaluator must see
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#5: Derive a property from every correctness property stated in the specification; a stated property with no executable test is an `unproven-property` finding
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#6: Pair every parser or serialiser with a round-trip property; forbid asserting round-trip fidelity by example alone
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#7: Pair every ordering, dedup, or aggregation rule with an invariant or metamorphic property
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#8: State each property's class explicitly — round trip, invariant, metamorphic, idempotence, confluence, error condition — so coverage gaps are visible by class rather than by count
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#9: Set a minimum iteration count per property and keep shrinking enabled; a property run once is an example test wearing a costume
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#10: Emit one Evidence Reference per satisfied VCC, carrying the named check, the recorded result, and the surface (always `authoring` during execution)
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#11: Forbid emitting an Evidence Reference for a check that was not run in this task
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#12: Forbid an Evidence Reference whose recorded result is an assertion that a result exists
executionRuleCatalog.checkpoint--recovery#1: Long runs outlive working context. A run that cannot resume is a run that must restart, and restarting re-spends every token already spent.
executionRuleCatalog.checkpoint--recovery#2: Persist run state — task states, transitions with reasons, Evidence References, findings, budget consumption — outside working context after every terminal transition
executionRuleCatalog.checkpoint--recovery#3: Checkpoint before approaching the context bound; forbid discovering a compaction boundary by losing work at it
executionRuleCatalog.checkpoint--recovery#4: On resume, re-establish position from persisted state rather than from memory of prior context, and re-verify the current artifact state before continuing a partially applied task
executionRuleCatalog.checkpoint--recovery#5: Treat a partially applied task as `failed` with recorded partial state, not as `in-progress`, so recovery decides explicitly whether to resume or re-derive
executionRuleCatalog.checkpoint--recovery#6: Forbid a recovery path that re-dispatches a `verified` task; re-verification is a re-derivation and resets the task explicitly
executionRuleCatalog.checkpoint--recovery#7: Record enough in each transition that a reader who followed none of the run can reconstruct what happened and why
executionRuleCatalog.human-in-the-loop-gates#1: Some decisions an agent must not make alone, regardless of confidence.
executionRuleCatalog.human-in-the-loop-gates#2: Forbid inferring, defaulting, scheduling, or simulating an Operator decision; an absent decision is a `blocked` state, never an assumed yes
executionRuleCatalog.human-in-the-loop-gates#3: Present a gate with the decision, the options, and the consequence of each; forbid escalating with a question the Operator cannot answer from what was surfaced
executionRuleCatalog.human-in-the-loop-gates#4: Forbid bundling an unrelated change into a gated task while waiting; a blocked task stays blocked
executionRuleCatalog.human-in-the-loop-gates#5: Record the Operator decision reference on the transition it authorises, so the authorisation is auditable later
executionRuleCatalog.dependency-ordered-integration#2: Classify each unit as `pending`, `already-integrated`, `superseded`, `integrated`, or `blocked`; forbid reintegrating an equivalent change or replacing newer canonical behavior with an older unit
executionRuleCatalog.dependency-ordered-integration#3: Build a directed acyclic graph from declared unit dependencies; a cycle is an `integration-order-cycle`, and integrating a unit before a dependency is `integration-before-dependency`
executionRuleCatalog.dependency-ordered-integration#4: Dispatch ready units in deterministic waves only when their write scopes are disjoint; serialize overlapping source owners even when their dependency sets differ
executionRuleCatalog.dependency-ordered-integration#6: Integrate shared control, contract, and source owners before consumers, generated projections, mirrors, or release candidates; source ownership, not repository or list position, determines order
executionRuleCatalog.dependency-ordered-integration#7: Rebase or merge the current canonical frontier into the owned mutation lane, resolve conflicts at the source owner, run named checks, and enter through protected integration without bypass
executionRuleCatalog.dependency-ordered-integration#8: Require every review-request or equivalent protected-integration record to be rendered from the repository-owned template, to bind the current canonical base revision at creation or update time, and to declare a scope token exactly equal to the admitted semantic scope; when a branch-segment projection exists, that scope token must equal the projected branch-scope segment as well
executionRuleCatalog.dependency-ordered-integration#9: When a commit push succeeds but the review-ready boundary fails closed because a cloud verifier momentarily resolves a different protected-review head, solve that drift only in the authority-owning source module by revalidating the unchanged claim, review-request, and intended reviewed head, then rerunning the same bounded verifier-and-transition path; downstream fence rewrites, projection patches, synthetic rebases, or alternate transition selection are forbidden
executionRuleCatalog.dependency-ordered-integration#10: Require the protected merge revision and its exact-canonical checks before advancing the frontier; a green task head alone is `canonical-frontier-unverified`
executionRuleCatalog.dependency-ordered-integration#12: Require runtime convergence when a unit declares runtime impact; keep source, exact-canonical, runtime, and delivery evidence as separate receipts
executionRuleCatalog.canonical-integration--recoverable-clean: Classify the candidate as `delta`, `already-integrated`, `superseded-with-value`, or `blocked`: compute file delta against the current canonical tree and separately prove commit reachability or semantic supersession, because zero file diff alone does not prove that unique history is disposable

Route every `delta` candidate through the repository's protected review and integration adapter; forbid direct canonical mutation, protection bypass, history rewrite, or substituting a local merge result for the protected integration receipt

After protected integration, refetch the canonical remote ref, attach or fast-forward the canonical local ref to that exact revision, and require a clean status plus zero file diff between their trees; a stale remote-tracking projection, merely green candidate check, or matching commit message is not canonical closure

Before removing a worktree or deleting a ref, prove either that its complete value is reachable from the canonical remote ref or that an immutable recovery object contains its exact revision, tree, local-only commits, index state, and ordinary untracked bytes and has passed an independent restore or integrity check

Forbid unrecoverable discard: do not force-remove a dirty worktree, delete an unpreserved unique ref, drop a stash, erase an untracked artifact, reset away authored state, expire a recovery object, or prune unreachable objects when the preservation proof is absent, stale, ambiguous, or unverifiable

Delete a stale local candidate ref only after canonical inclusion is proven or after its verified recovery locator and digest are recorded in the cleanup receipt; keep every unrelated, active, ambiguous, open-review, or value-bearing ref unchanged

Make cleanup adaptive to the observed inventory: a no-worktree lane closes as a ref-only operation, an already-integrated zero-delta lane closes without a synthetic merge, and a value-bearing lane remains preserved until its own protected integration or explicit recoverable retirement completes

Emit one terminal receipt that binds the canonical remote and local revisions, zero file delta, clean status, removed worktree identities, deleted local refs, pruned metadata, retained recovery locators, and untouched out-of-scope inventory; forbid reporting closure unless the canonical local ref equals the canonical remote ref and every requested effect is evidenced
executionRuleCatalog.end-to-end-release-lifecycle-protocol#2: Seal one immutable candidate from the exact final Release Frontier, including source, transitive dependencies, policy, schema, catalog, generated projections, state contract, target, review, artifact, manifest, and rollback identities
executionRuleCatalog.end-to-end-release-lifecycle-protocol#3: Inventory every pre-existing non-canonical lane or worktree before candidate sealing and classify each exact item as `keep`, `port`, or `drop`, with its identity, scope, evidence, and rationale recorded
executionRuleCatalog.end-to-end-release-lifecycle-protocol#4: Preserve every `keep` item untouched, require every `port` item to reach protected integration before the candidate can claim frontier closure, and allow `drop` only after exact no-remaining-value proof plus the cleanup authority that removes it
executionRuleCatalog.end-to-end-release-lifecycle-protocol#6: Require a current Runtime Review Receipt before prompting and a separate authenticated human decision for the exact candidate and target before deployment
executionRuleCatalog.end-to-end-release-lifecycle-protocol#7: Fence one canonical release-owner checkout per repository from candidate sealing until the authorization interaction terminates or the run is retired; it must stay attached to the exact protected revision used for review, and branch switching, repurposing, or local-ref drift in that owner invalidates prompt readiness until the owner is reattached, refetched, and revalidated
executionRuleCatalog.end-to-end-release-lifecycle-protocol#8: Require terminal authorization automation to follow a sequential prompt handshake: capture the exact candidate-bound reply emitted by the prompt formatter, wait for the live input prompt, then send that exact reply; precomputed, reordered, promptless, or partially matched input creates no authorization evidence
executionRuleCatalog.end-to-end-release-lifecycle-protocol#9: Keep interaction, authority, deployment, state reconciliation, verification, publication, rollback, and cleanup as replaceable adapter ports with typed inputs and receipts
executionRuleCatalog.end-to-end-release-lifecycle-protocol#10: Invalidate the affected receipt chain on any identity movement; cancel or retire stale unapproved runs rather than retargeting, rebuilding, or reusing authorization
executionRuleCatalog.end-to-end-release-lifecycle-protocol#11: Verify immutable deployment identity, authoritative state readback, public transports, browser behavior, and client-cache convergence as separate claims where the target profile requires them
executionRuleCatalog.end-to-end-release-lifecycle-protocol#12: Publish mirrors only after the Live Verification Receipt exists; remove only clean, integrated, completion-proven task lanes and preserve all unrelated work
executionRuleCatalog.runtime-readiness-enforcement#1: Runtime readiness is a derived claim over one immutable execution input and its joined evidence; never infer it from document status, source existence, review labels, or delivery state. The separately loadable [Behavioral Conformance Runtime Module](./agentic-sdlc-conformance-runtime.md) owns the stage-gate evidence and receipt contract; the [Repository Runtime Readiness Module](./agentic-sdlc-repository-runtime-readiness.md) owns the bounded local-first repository audit profile.
executionRuleCatalog.runtime-readiness-enforcement#2: Require typed inputs and outputs, bounded orchestration, independent evaluation, named checks with recorded results, cost and fallback evidence, and closed mutation and deployment gates before deriving `runtime-ready`
executionRuleCatalog.runtime-readiness-enforcement#3: Keep source validation, canonical runtime, protected integration, and deployed proof as separate claims; forbid one green layer from promoting another
executionRuleCatalog.runtime-readiness-enforcement#4: Keep scoped authoring admission, runtime readiness, and lifecycle readiness as independent results; never turn preserved disjoint work or an occupied runtime into a false global verdict
executionRuleCatalog.runtime-readiness-enforcement#5: Emit `runtime-readiness-unproven` at `blocker` severity when a required receipt, join, budget, check, evaluator, dependency, or boundary proof is absent or stale
executionRuleCatalog.runtime-readiness-enforcement#6: Require repository-owned stage gates to consume operation-derived evidence and emit digest-bound receipts for admission, review, integration, runtime, candidate, authorization, deployment, and publication; expose a deterministic evaluator command that exits zero only when every required proof joins, and forbid `npx`, `latest`, or dynamic resolution from creating policy identity, gate authority, or runtime-readiness proof
executionRuleCatalog.execution-conformance-findings#1: Treat this enumeration as the single source of truth for execution-domain finding names; forbid redefining any authoring-domain type here
executionRuleCatalog.execution-conformance-findings#2: Anchor every finding to the Rule ID of the violated rule in this set, per the authoring set's Rule Identity & Classification
executionRuleCatalog.execution-conformance-findings#3: Report a zero count for every type with no finding; an omitted row is indistinguishable from an unchecked rule
executionRuleCatalog.execution-load-budget#1: Load by section anchor for the current stage; forbid loading the whole set as a precondition for a single-stage action
executionRuleCatalog.execution-load-budget#2: Record this set's load cost in the per-run token total alongside the authoring set's; the cost of governing the work is part of the cost of the work
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#2: **Specification baselined** with zero open `blocker` findings in the authoring domain
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#3: **Evaluator mechanism named** and demonstrably distinct from the Implementer
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#4: **Every task traced** to at least one VCC; every VCC covered by at least one task; bridge coverage ratio reported
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#5: **Dependency graph acyclic**; waves contain no two tasks writing the same artifact
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#6: **Collaboration identity complete when concurrent mutation applies**; authoritative future write scopes, distinct lanes, and exact fences are present without path inference; current local leases are required only for local mutation-capable projections
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#8: **When additive concurrent authoring is requested, scoped lane admitted and preserved**; joined receipts bind exact source/scope, cloud/local/shared-state digests, target/atomic result, final active claim evidence, zero candidate-caused collateral mutation, `authoringAdmission: admitted`, and claim-plus-local-lease revalidation at first consumption
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#9: **Reviewed delivery authority is exact when protected integration applies**; one current `delivery-authorized` receipt binds the unchanged reviewed revision, scope, claim, lease epoch, fence, ledger revision, and review/check evidence without reopening authoring or granting deployment authority
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#10: **All four budgets stated** per task, with a circuit-breaker condition
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#11: **Capability grants stated** per task at the narrowest sufficient class; write scope declared
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#12: **Named check stated** per task before dispatch
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#13: **Property obligations identified** per stated correctness property, with class named
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#14: Named check run and its recorded result surfaced
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#15: Existing verification lane run, not only the task's own check
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#16: Artifacts changed enumerated, including incidental changes
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#17: Budget consumption recorded against all four bounds
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#18: Verdict issued by the Evaluator, never the Implementer
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#19: Evidence Reference emitted per satisfied VCC, with surface recorded
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#20: State transition recorded with the role that made it and a reason where terminal
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#21: **Runtime readiness derived** by the deterministic evaluator from one immutable input and joined, layer-specific proof; every missing or stale obligation fails closed
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#22: **Every task in a terminal state**; no task left `in-progress`
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#23: Every `failed`, `blocked`, and `abandoned` task carries a reason
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#24: **Rungs re-derived** from the emitted Evidence References; no rung authored by hand
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#25: **Finding set emitted** across both domains, deduplicated, ordered, with zero counts reported
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#26: **Finding set compared** to the prior run; any new `blocker` treated as a regression
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#27: **Run state persisted** such that an independent reader can reconstruct the run
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#28: **Per-run consumption compared** to the specification's token budget
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#29: **No boundary crossed**: every task ran in the `authoring` lane; every Deploy Boundary still reads `closed` absent an Operator instruction
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#30: **Integration order closed**: every unit is terminal, dependencies preceded consumers, no equivalent or superseded unit was re-merged, and exact-canonical checks advanced each frontier
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#31: **Protected review metadata exact**: the repository-owned review-request template is instantiated, the current canonical base revision is recorded, and the declared scope token equals the admitted semantic scope and any projected branch-scope segment
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#33: **Authorization prompt runtime-ready**: candidate, source, release run, and controlled review-surface locator are revalidated from the current Runtime Review Receipt before the prompt is emitted; the prompt identifies its canonical portable formatter as `agentic-canvas-os/scripts/production-release-authorization-contract.mjs` and, directly after its loopback locator, prints the runtime-resolved local formatter source path
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#34: **Canonical release owner stable**: from candidate sealing through authorization interaction, one canonical release-owner checkout stays on the exact protected revision used for review; any branch flip or local-ref drift retires or blocks the run until the owner is restored and the receipt chain is refreshed
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#35: **Receipt chain joined**: Integration, Runtime Review, Candidate, Authorization Interaction, Human Authorization, Deployment, State Reconciliation, Live Verification, Publication, and Rollback receipts join by exact digest where each stage applies
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#36: **Overlapping work preserved**: every pre-existing non-canonical work item is content-bound and accounted for; overlapping items remain retained with recovery handles, while any restored disjoint item matches its captured state exactly
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#37: **Keep / port / drop inventory closed**: every pre-existing non-canonical lane or worktree is classified by exact identity; `keep` items remain preserved, `port` items integrate before candidate sealing, and `drop` items are removed only with value-closure proof plus cleanup authority
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#39: **Candidate closure exact**: canonical source, all transitive dependencies, policy, target, review, artifact, manifest, and candidate digests agree
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#40: **Human authorization exact**: the interaction receipt proves the configured transport, browser dependency, exact challenge response, and authenticated actor; the authority adapter records the same human decision for that candidate and target
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#42: **Controller singular and idempotent**: one target-scoped controller owns deployment; duplicate dispatch resolves to the same result or fails closed
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#43: **No drift or rebuild**: current evidence still matches the authorized candidate byte-for-byte; otherwise authorization is invalid and forward deployment remains blocked
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#44: **State reconciled**: state changes are bounded and idempotent, direct readback matches expected counts and content, and code and state rollback dispositions remain separate
executionRuleCatalog.validation-checklist#45: **Transports proven separately**: immutable origin, required public routes, authoritative state readback, browser behavior, client-cache convergence, and publication each carry their own evidence where applicable
executionRuleCatalog.anti-pattern-guards#1: ❌ Tasks invented at task-authoring time to cover behaviour the specification never stated → ✅ Every task derived from a VCC; a behaviour gap returned to the authoring loop as a specification defect
executionRuleCatalog.anti-pattern-guards#2: → ✅ Execution confined to the authoring lane; promotion is the Deploy Boundary's job and never a task
executionRuleCatalog.mantra-application#1: **Specification grounds**: a task with no VCC behind it is work no rung will credit, so the bridge is a derivation and never a fresh authoring act
